name: PCA9554 I/O Expander
description: The PCA9554 component allows you to use a variety of I/O expanders in ESPHome that use the [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c/) for communication. Once configured, you can use any of the IO pins (up to 16) with your projects. Within ESPHome they emulate a real internal GPIO pin and can therefore be used with many of ESPHome's components such as the GPIO binary sensor or GPIO switch. Any option accepting a [Pin Schema](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types/#pin-schema) can theoretically be used, but some more complicated components that do communication through this I/O expander will not work.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: The I²C address of the device; see the table above. Defaults to the lowest address of the selected `device`, with all address pins low: `0x20` for most parts, `0x38` for the PCA9534A and PCA9554A, `0x41` for the PCA9536 and `0x70` for the PCA9538 and PCAL9538.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: The id to use for this `pca9554` component.

config_entries.label: Interrupt Pin
config_entries.description: The pin connected to the INT output of the expander. When configured, the component becomes interrupt-driven instead of polling: it only reads the chip when a pin actually changes state, significantly reducing I²C bus traffic and CPU usage. The INT pin is active-low and open-drain, so an external or internal pull-up resistor is required. Must be an internal GPIO pin (not another expander pin). On the PCAL parts every input pin asserts INT and every output pin is masked, so no per-pin setup is needed.

config_entries.label: Mode
config_entries.description: Pin mode flags (input / output / pullup / pulldown / open_drain). Combine flags as needed — e.g. input + pullup for a button pulled to VCC.

config_entries.label: Open Drain
config_entries.description: Set the open drain mode flag.

config_entries.label: Inverted
config_entries.description: Invert the logical level. ``true`` swaps high/low in software so an active-low button reads as active when grounded.

config_entries.label: Device
config_entries.description: The part in use, one of the names in the table above. Defaults to `PCA9554`, or to the plain part with the pins given by `pin_count`.

config_entries.label: Pin Count
config_entries.description: The number of pins of the expander, `4`, `8` or `16`, for configurations that predate `device`. With `device` set it may be left out; if both are given they must agree.
